review_kind: Static inspection of the six exact reference patches and relevant base source; no new implementation or test execution.
conclusion: No additional clear implementation blocker identified in this static pass. The references need independent integration review and the explicitly listed compatibility decisions; individual prior test results do not establish a qualified combined release.

patches.scope: Core signature-family binding before Git verifier dispatch; affects every caller of the shared trusted-signature helper.
limitations: Adds a 65,536-byte TOTAL commit-object cap at trusted_git.verify_signature, counting headers, signature and message. This is a new direct-helper input restriction. Normal publication verification already has the same total-object cap in publication_protocol.commit (MAX_MESSAGE=65536), reached through commit_identity/verify_shape before signature verification; do not describe this as a newly lowered cap for ordinary discovered editions.

Requires exactly one gpgsig header, rejects other gpgsig-prefixed headers, and accepts only the specified SSH or OpenPGP armor with a single BEGIN marker and exact final END line. These explicit syntax restrictions are separate from the required signature-family binding and may be narrower than Git backend parsing of historical input.
Retains inherited Git environment handling except GIT_GRAFT_FILE. The extractor environment cleanup in patch 05 does not harden these core Git operations.
independent_review: Confirm the supported historical signature encodings and alternate-header policy before adoption. Inspect retained accepted history, including direct signature-helper use, rather than treating the new armor tests as proof of complete compatibility.
Keep the crucial mismatch rejection before backend dispatch. Reconcile the duplicated 64 KiB constants and document that the limit applies to the whole commit object.

Requalify explicit SSH and OpenPGP trust, both cross-family rejection directions, and preservation/discovery/rendering consumers on the integration revision. New source restrictions require an explicit compatibility decision; do not rewrite accepted source history to accommodate them.

patches.scope: Generator compatibility with source-approved mailto query parameters and shared external-URI syntax validation.
limitations: Intentionally partial parity: core valid_source_link still accepts credential-bearing HTTPS URLs while the renderer still refuses them. The reference preserves that renderer restriction and leaves core source acceptance unchanged.

Changing the core predicate to reject those historical URLs would retroactively reject some previously accepted signed inputs; simply widening the renderer would weaken its existing explicit credential policy.

A later source edit cannot repair an unrenderable historical edition because site generation traverses accepted history. The included regression covers that failure mode for mailto links, not every possible source/renderer contract difference.
independent_review: Retain generator-to-core authority direction; the generator consumes the core URI predicate and does not define publication eligibility.
Resolve credential URL handling and any migration/versioning policy separately. Keep it visible as an unresolved recommendation, not a completed fix.
Review accepted-link compatibility for manuscript and supporting GFM while preserving the stricter media destination policy.

patches.scope: Generator hosted-private-preview process replacement and in-process rollback to last-good output.
limitations: Uses stop/start on one port, so rollback improves recovery without guaranteeing uninterrupted connections or zero downtime.
A restored last-good listener still reports the attempted refresh as failed. This preserves failed health status instead of claiming the candidate revision was adopted.
Rollback metadata and storage values are retained in memory. The patch does not add durable crash recovery, process-restart restoration, or a policy for expiring credentials.
The new terminate/kill/reap bounds cover Preview.close. Existing preview.start_server and serve have separate termination paths that this patch does not comprehensively redesign.
independent_review: Confirm last-good authentication and storage credentials are still usable when replayed; preserve private session isolation and no-store behavior.
Review dual startup failure, termination failure, shutdown, and deletion ordering with the deployment supervisor and intended platform.
Do not equate process rollback with private staged-asset retention; the separate garbage-collection/active-draft recommendation remains open.

patches.scope: Extractor private-output custody, independent of ambient Git routing and indeterminate Git failures.
limitations: Recognizes repository absence through one exact Git diagnostic under forced LC_ALL=C. Verified with Git 2.56.1; changed wording on another supported version will conservatively refuse output rather than authorize it.
Any ancestor .git marker is enough to refuse output, including unreadable or invalid repository markers. This deliberately favors privacy over permissive recovery from broken repositories.

Preserves the original outside-worktree distinction: a genuine successful false reply without a .git ancestor remains allowed, including bare-repository contexts. It does not establish a broader prohibition on every directory containing Git data.
Sanitizes Git environment only for this custody check. It neither changes publication authority nor repairs other core Git invocation policies.
independent_review: Qualify the absence diagnostic and path behavior on the supported Git/platform matrix; keep unknown failures fail-closed.
Confirm intended policy for bare repositories and Git environment overrides. Preserve ordinary external output, linked-worktree rejection, exclusive creation, and mode 0600.
Treat the check as local path custody using the existing exclusive-create model, not as a new filesystem transaction or hostile concurrent-directory defense.

patches.scope: Repository checkout-byte stability for tracked core and generator runtime files used in renderer identity.
limitations: text=auto eol=lf applies to the tracked runtime roots. It does not establish byte stability for untracked/generated/vendor-installed inputs, npm-supplied SQLite runtime files, compiler versions, or dependency versions.
Does not retroactively rewrite existing blobs or already-modified working files; verify from a clean integration checkout.
The regression intentionally reads HEAD with ls-tree/cat-file, including attributes. Running it on an uncommitted patch tests the previous commit rather than the staged candidate.
independent_review: Run this regression against an actual integration commit or equivalent disposable commit containing the patch.
Confirm binary autodetection and any future explicit nested attributes for all tracked runtime input types; avoid blanket history renormalization.
Retain separate artifact/runtime qualification. The patch repairs checkout drift, not all sources of renderer fingerprint differences.

patches.scope: Documented initializer package pinning and an executable check on those examples.
limitations: Documentation-only execution pin: users must replace reviewed-sha with the reviewed full commit and use the same value in GUAVAJAM_TOOL_REF.
Does not add runtime enforcement that the executing initializer package matches GUAVAJAM_TOOL_REF, alter already-created repositories, or prove the chosen revision was reviewed.
The policy test checks command-reference syntax and intra-example consistency, not live package retrieval or deployment qualification.
independent_review: Keep the onboarding example aligned with the actual release-install procedure and the repository minimal-prose policy.
If runtime package/reference equality becomes a release requirement, specify and implement it separately; do not claim this documentation patch enforces it.

cross_package_review: All six patches remain independently reviewable. No changed-path overlap or newly reversed package dependency is apparent from their diffs; textual independence does not prove runtime integration compatibility.

Patch 01 changes a shared trust helper consumed by discovery, signed rendering, assets and source preservation. Its family-binding security fix and its stricter accepted input syntax must be reviewed as distinct claims.

Patches 02 and 01 both affect the ability to regenerate retained history. Inventory existing accepted sources before changing those contracts; a source-edit-only workaround is insufficient for immutable historical editions.

Patches 01, 02 and 04 change runtime bytes hashed by renderer_identity; rebuilding disposable views or caches is expected. Patch 06 stabilizes checkout bytes but does not promise unchanged renderer fingerprints after code changes.

The contribution is a nonauthoritative implementation reference. Rebase/adapt to the current target revision, review the combined diff, and run required package, boundary, artifact and deployment gates on the final integration commit.

The six code/documentation patches do not themselves close the active-draft garbage-collection issue, external release/branch enforcement decisions, provider rehearsal, or deferred spoken screen-reader qualification.
